result.title: Goal-Driven Autonomous Optical Experimentation via a Self-Recursive Hardware-Software Harness
result.summary: We propose goal-driven self-recursive optical research in which agents use physical evidence to revise the hardware, software, models, and protocols used to pursue a scientific goal. The framework can be instantiated with different stimulus systems and measurement devices. We formalize its updates and derive a relation between physical attainability, command access, and model approximation error. We demonstrate the concept in an optical see-through color-matching case study using an iPad, RayNeo X3 glasses, and a TOP 300 probe coupled to a CAS140D spectroradiometer, both from Instrument Systems. A revised glasses application adds USB-controlled RGB holds and frame acknowledgements, keeping model-generated colors displayed during spectral acquisition. The interface passes 12 live control checks. Spectral feedback reduces one target color difference from 19.756 to 1.211 ΔE_76^*; all five targets improve in a separate comparison. These measurements demonstrate the concept in one configuration. The resulting software and protocols remain available for subsequent investigations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「目标驱动的自递归光学研究」框架，让智能体依据物理测量证据迭代修订硬件、软件、模型与协议，并在 iPad 与 AR 眼镜的色匹配案例中用光谱反馈验证该闭环。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「采证—修订模型/协议」的闭环及物理可达性、命令访问权限与模型近似误差的关系式，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据获取、迭代状态修订与停止决策提供问题表述参考，但任务域相距较远，仅供核查。
